key_insight: Across ABO2 oxides, delafossite and ordered rock-salt variants can compete with infinite-layer phases in stability, especially for nickelates, palladates, and platinate analogs.
engineering_relevance: This maps which compositions and dopants are most likely to stabilize target oxide phases, helping guide synthesis of superconducting or correlated-electron materials.
method: High-throughput first-principles (DFT) screening of AB O2 oxides
Phase-diagram comparison of infinite-layer, delafossite, and ordered rock-salt structures
Electronic-structure analysis of Fermi-surface orbital character
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a computed stability survey across the periodic table, showing delafossite competitiveness and identifying La-Ni as the thermodynamic optimum for the infinite-layer motif.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on thermodynamic first-principles predictions, so actual film growth, strain, and substrate effects may shift which phase is experimentally realized.
paper_title: Delafossites as an unexpected competing phase to infinite-layer oxides
